title: HollyShorts Film Festival 2025
deck: A 21st anniversary, drawn in pencil first.
lede: The 21st anniversary poster began on an easel, in pencil, then moved through a sketchbook of color studies. From there it spread to badges, merchandise, a metal award and three events.
challenge: The 21st HollyShorts Film Festival, at the TCL Chinese Theatres in 2025, needed its official anniversary poster and everything that follows from one: merchandise, badges, the award and the production design of three events, the festival, the Alta Global Media Film Summit and the award show.
work: The poster is original art. It was drawn in pencil on an easel, worked out in a sketchbook of color studies and concept drawings, and tested in a color sketch of the full composition before the final. An annotated poster guide set out how the art would travel.

Production design followed the same route: an annotated concept sketch, an electronic proof from Distinctive Event Solutions, and printed signage staged for setup. It covered step-and-repeats, billboards, the theater lobby, event signage, on-screen creative and the award show. On site, the poster art became a backdrop framed by lit palm trees, ran on the LED marquee and filled the theater screen before each program.

There were eight badge designs. Merchandise ran from tees and a windbreaker to a bucket hat, shorts, socks, mugs and postcards. The award was designed and made with Revello Metal in Long Beach, California.
system: Made in metal in Long Beach.
Step-and-repeats, billboards, the lobby, signs and screens.
deliverables: Merchandise: tees, windbreaker, bucket hat, shorts, socks, mugs, postcards
Step-and-repeats, billboards, theater lobby, event signage, on-screen creative
Award show and Film Summit production design
credits: Dalton Corr: art direction, poster art, merchandise, badges, award design, production design
Revello Metal, Long Beach: award fabrication
press: HollyShorts.com: the 21st anniversary poster unveiled, with a design credit.
Animation Magazine: the 21st edition lineup and poster.
The festival was covered by Deadline, League of Filmmakers and Moviejawn.
